claims.text: The protective coating has an FCC/BCC high-entropy-alloy microstructure.
The coating's creep resistance under continuous loading is governed by dynamic microstructural evolution.
Dislocation formation and evolution contribute to creep resistance.
Grain-boundary evolution contributes to creep resistance.
Dislocations and grain boundaries impede dislocation glide.
Interaction of dislocations with grain boundaries leads to work hardening.
Work hardening caused by dislocation–grain-boundary interactions increases creep resistance.
Continuous loading will increase dislocation density relative to the starting microstructure.
Continuous loading will produce grain-boundary strengthening relative to the starting microstructure.
The loading-induced microstructural changes will improve creep resistance relative to the starting baseline.
Temperature, stress, and strain rate define boundaries beyond which the microstructure and creep resistance may degrade.
In-situ TEM under continuous loading can directly observe the microstructural changes associated with creep.

contradictions.description: The predicted outcome compares creep resistance during continuous loading with a baseline described as being without continuous loading. Because creep resistance must be assessed under a load protocol, this baseline is not directly comparable as stated.
